---
title: "What does the redesigned aircraft look like next to the original?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Show code"
# The constrained design, not the unconstrained one: it is the only one of the
# two that is a credible shape, and it is what "the redesign" means here.
redesign = constrained_redesign()


def planform(span, chords):
    """Station, leading edge and trailing edge for the quarter-chord-straight wing."""
    stations = np.array([float(f) * span / 2 for f in STATION_FRACTION])
    chords = np.array([float(c) for c in chords])
    leading = WING_LE_X + 0.25 * (chords[0] - chords)
    return stations, leading, leading + chords


def outline(stations, leading, trailing):
    """One semi-span as a closed loop: out along the leading edge, back along the trailing."""
    span_wise = np.concatenate([stations, stations[::-1], stations[:1]])
    stream_wise = np.concatenate([leading, trailing[::-1], leading[:1]])
    return span_wise, stream_wise


baseline_geometry = planform(SPAN, STATION_C)
redesign_geometry = planform(redesign["span"], redesign["chords"])

baseline_ratio = SPAN ** 2 / float(WING.area())
outer_fraction = (1.0 - STATION_FRACTION[-2]) * 100

# The comparison is only meaningful if area really is held: a longer wing that
# also grew would be a different aeroplane, not a redesign of this one.
assert abs(redesign["area"] / float(WING.area()) - 1) < 0.01, "wing area moved"
```

**Answer.** Same area, longer and sharper (@fig-geometry). Span grows
`{python} f"{SPAN:.2f}"` → [`{python} f"{redesign['span']:.2f}"`]{.key} m and
aspect ratio `{python} f"{baseline_ratio:.1f}"` →
[`{python} f"{redesign['aspect_ratio']:.1f}"`]{.key}, bought by moving chord
inboard: the root widens to [`{python} f"{redesign['chords'][0]:.3f}"`]{.key} m
while the outer `{python} f"{outer_fraction:.0f}"`% of span holds a constant
[`{python} f"{redesign['chords'][-1]:.3f}"`]{.key} m, because the Reynolds floor
pins the tip. Washout covers a similar range but sits nose-up inboard and flat
outboard.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Chordwise scale is exaggerated

At true proportions an 18 m wing of 0.7 m mean chord is a line. The spanwise and
chordwise axes are scaled differently so the planform change can be seen at all.
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-geometry
#| fig-cap: "The original wing and the redesign, overlaid. Above, planform with both semi-spans; the original is filled, the redesign outlined. Below, twist against distance from the centreline. Fuselage and tail are unchanged and are not drawn."
fig, (ax_plan, ax_twist) = plt.subplots(
    2, 1, figsize=(7.0, 4.6), height_ratios=[2.1, 1.0])

for (stations, leading, trailing), label, colour, filled in [
    (baseline_geometry, "Original", "C2", True),
    (redesign_geometry, "Redesign", "C0", False),
]:
    span_wise, stream_wise = outline(stations, leading, trailing)
    for side in (1, -1):
        if filled:
            ax_plan.fill(side * span_wise, stream_wise, color=colour,
                         alpha=0.20, zorder=2)
        ax_plan.plot(side * span_wise, stream_wise, color=colour, lw=1.6,
                     zorder=3, label=label if side == 1 else None)

ax_plan.invert_yaxis()
ax_plan.set_ylabel("Streamwise [m]")
ax_plan.set_xlabel("Distance from centreline [m]")
ax_plan.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax_plan.legend(loc="lower right")

for stations, twists, label, colour in [
    (baseline_geometry[0], STATION_TWIST, "Original", "C2"),
    (redesign_geometry[0], redesign["twists"], "Redesign", "C0"),
]:
    ax_twist.plot(stations, [float(t) for t in twists], "-o", ms=4,
                  color=colour, label=label, zorder=3)

ax_twist.axhline(0, color="C2", lw=0.7, zorder=2)
ax_twist.set_ylabel("Twist [deg]")
ax_twist.set_xlabel("Distance from centreline [m]")
ax_twist.grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
